
# Netflix Viewing Data

  
## Task 1-3: Data Acquisition, Cleaning and Preparation
```{r}
  library(tidyverse)
  library(rvest)

load_netflix_data <- function(){

  library(tidyverse)
  library(rvest)
  library(readxl)
  library(fs)
  
  data_dir <- path("data", "mp01")
    
  if(!dir_exists(data_dir)){
    dir_create(data_dir, showWarnings=FALSE, recurse=TRUE)
  }
  
  NETFLIX_URLS <- list(
    `2023H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-a-netflix-engagement-report",
    `2023H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2023",
    `2024H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2024",
    `2024H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2024",
    `2025H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2025",
    `2025H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2025",
    `2026H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2026"
  )
  
  download_if_needed <- function(url, local){
    if(!file_exists(local)){
      download.file(url, local, quiet = TRUE, mode = "wb")
    }
    
    return(local)
  }
    
  NETFLIX_URLS |> 
    map(read_html) |> 
    map(html_element, xpath = "//a[contains(@href, '.xlsx')]") |> 
    map_chr(html_attr, "href") |> 
    enframe("period", "url") |> 
   mutate(path = path(data_dir, paste0(period, ".xlsx")), 
          path = map2(url, path, download_if_needed), 
          data = map(path, read_excel, skip=3, na="*"), 
          data = map(data, \(x) x |> mutate(`Release Date` = as.Date(`Release Date`)))) |>
    unnest(data) |> 
    select(-url, -path) |> 
    mutate(year=str_sub(period, 1, 4), 
           half=str_sub(period, start=6), 
           period_start = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 1, 7), 1), 
           period_end = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 6, 12), if_else(half==1, 30, 31))) |> 
    filter(!is.na(`Hours Viewed`)) |> 
    mutate(live_event = !is.na(Runtime) & str_detect(Runtime, "\\d+:\\d+\\*"), 
           clean_time = str_remove(Runtime, fixed("*")),
           Runtime = 60 * hour(hm(clean_time)) + minute(hm(clean_time))) |>
    select(-clean_time) |>
    mutate(Runtime = coalesce(Runtime, mean(Runtime, na.rm=TRUE)), 
           .by=Title, 
           Title = stringi::stri_trans_general(Title, "Latin-ASCII"),
           Title = str_remove(Title, " // .*"), 
           Title = str_remove(Title, "[^[:ascii:]].*"), 
           Title = str_trim(Title)) |>
    filter_out(Title == "") |>
    select(year, 
           period, 
           period_start, 
           period_end, 
           Title, 
           -half, 
           Runtime, 
           Views, 
           `Hours Viewed`, 
           `Release Date`,
           `Available Globally?`, 
           live_event)
}

NETFLIX_DATA <- load_netflix_data() |>
   rename(title = Title,
          runtime = Runtime,
          views = Views,
          hours_viewed = `Hours Viewed`,
          release_date = `Release Date`,
          available_globally = `Available Globally?`) |>
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(year),
    available_globally = available_globally =="Yes"
  )
```

## Task 4: Initial EDA Pass
```{r}
glimpse(NETFLIX_DATA)
summary(NETFLIX_DATA)
```
Based on the summary NETFLIX DATA, we can see that dataset contains 61892 records from year 2023 to 2026. And the runtime, views, and the release_date are missing 13085, 18198, and 35251 values respectively, especially release_date is missing for about 57% of records. This would use fewer records if we want to analyze the popularity based on the release year.

## Task 5: Exploratory Questions - Inline Values

### Question 1
```{r}
date_range <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  summarize(
    start = min(period_start, na.rm = TRUE),
    end = max(period_end, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

date_range
```
The dataset covers the period from `r date_range$start` to `r date_range$end`.

### Question 2
```{r}
title_count <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  summarize(n_titles = n_distinct(title))
```
The dataset covers `r title_count$n_titles` different shows and movies.

### Question 3
```{r}
bridgerton_hours <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  filter(str_detect(title, "Bridgerton")) |>
  summarize(total_hours = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE)) 
bridgerton_hours
```
A total of `r format(bridgerton_hours$total_hours, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",")` hours have been spent watching shows from the Bridgerton universe.

### Questio 4
```{r}
stranger_hours <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  filter(str_detect(title, "Stranger Things")) |>
  filter_out(str_detect(title, "Beyond Stranger Things")) |>
  filter_out(str_detect(title, "Fireplace")) |>
  summarize(total_hours = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE))

stranger_hours
```

A total of `r format(stranger_hours$total_hours, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",")` hours have been spent watching the five seasons of Stranger Things.

### Question 5
```{r}
top10_share <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  filter(period == "2026H1") |>
  arrange(desc(hours_viewed)) |>
  summarize(
    percentage = 100 * sum(hours_viewed[1:10], na.rm = TRUE) /
      sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

top10_share
```
In 2026H1, the percentage of total watch time spent on the Top 10 titles was about `r round(top10_share$percentage, 1)` %.

### Question 6
```{r}
global_share <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  summarize(
    by_title = n_distinct(title[available_globally %in% TRUE]) / n_distinct(title),
    by_hours = sum(hours_viewed[available_globally %in% TRUE], na.rm = TRUE) /
      sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

global_share
```
About `r round(100 * global_share$by_title, 1)`% of titles are globally available and `r round(100 * global_share$by_hours, 1)`% of the total hours viewed.

## Task 6: Exploratory Questions - Table Answers

### Question 1
```{r}
NETFLIX_DATA |>
  group_by(period, title) |>
  summarize(hours = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop_last") |>
  mutate(share = hours / sum(hours)) |>
  slice_max(hours, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Top Title in Each Period") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = hours, decimals = 0) |>
  gt::fmt_percent(columns = share, decimals = 1)
```

### Question 2
```{r}
NETFLIX_DATA |>
  group_by(period) |>
  summarize(
    titles = n_distinct(title),
    total_runtime = sum(runtime, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Catalog Size by Period") |>
    gt::fmt_number(columns = c(titles, total_runtime), decimals = 0) |>
  gt::cols_label(titles = "Titles", total_runtime = "Total runtime (minutes)")
```

### Question 3
```{r}
NETFLIX_DATA |>
  filter(!is.na(hours_viewed)) |>
  group_by(title) |>
  summarize(
    periods = n_distinct(period),
    average_hours = mean(hours_viewed),
    lowest_hours = min(hours_viewed)
  ) |>
  filter(periods == 7) |>
  slice_max(lowest_hours, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Consistently Popular Titles") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(average_hours, lowest_hours), decimals = 0)
```

### Question 4
```{r}
NETFLIX_DATA |>
  mutate(type = case_when(
    str_detect(title, "Season") | runtime > 240 ~ "Show",
    is.na(runtime) ~ "Unknown",
    .default = "Movie"
  )) |>
  group_by(period, type) |>
  summarize(hours = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop_last") |>
  mutate(share = hours / sum(hours)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(period, type, share) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = share) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Watch Time by Shows and Movies") |>
  gt::fmt_percent(columns = c(Show, Movie, Unknown), decimals = 1)
```

### Question 5
```{r}
NETFLIX_DATA |>
  mutate(type = if_else(live_event, "Live", "Pre-taped")) |>
  group_by(type) |>
  summarize(
    titles = n(),
    average_hours = mean(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE),
    top_tier_hours = mean(
      hours_viewed[hours_viewed >= quantile(hours_viewed, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE)],
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Live vs. Pre-taped Content") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(titles, average_hours, top_tier_hours), decimals = 0)
```

### Calculation for Task 7
```{r}
memo_shares <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  filter(period == "2026H1") |>
  mutate(type = case_when(
    str_detect(title, "Season") | runtime > 240 ~ "Show",
    is.na(runtime) ~ "Unknown",
    .default = "Movie"
  )) |>
  group_by(type) |>
  summarize(hours = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * hours / sum(hours))
```

## Task 7: Corporate Strategy Memo

**To: Netflix Management**

According to the dataset and table, we have a few content recommendations for the coming year 2027 based on wattime trends from 2023 H1 to 2026 H1.

First, we found that the watch time percentage for shows was consistently higher than for movies from 2023 H1 to 2026 H1. For example, in 2026 H1, watch time for shows was `r round(memo_shares$pct[memo_shares$type == "Show"], 1) `%, while movies only made up `r round(memo_shares$pct[memo_shares$type =="Movie"], 1) `%.Because shows tend to generate higher viewership, I suggest Netflix release more shows by 2027.

Second, in 2026 H1, the Top 10 title is for only about `r round(top10_share$percentage, 1) `% of total watch time. This shows that viewers are not just watching popular trending title; instead, they are watching content based on their personal preference across the Netflix platform. So, Netflix should monitor which specific show genres appeal to different viewer segments and invest in a wider variety of show types.

Also, we need to notice a limitation that is higher watch time doesn't mean higher profit, since production costs for shows can be high. So, we should also consider production costs and revenue metrics.
